## Methods reported in the three papers

| Paper | Method | Params | mIoU | Claimed design story |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| paper_1.pdf | Method A — convolutional segmentation | 2.5M | 73.27 | Strong mid-budget convolutional baseline [paper_1.pdf, p.1] |
| paper_2.pdf | Method B — attention segmentation | 3.2M | 76.0 | Attention gives the highest quality, at the highest cost [paper_2.pdf, p.1] |
| paper_3.pdf | Method C — compact convolution baseline | 2.0M | 70.0 | Cheapest configuration; lower quality [paper_3.pdf, p.1] |

All three papers describe the same fixture benchmark and evaluation protocol, and all three explicitly frame their claims as a **descriptive quality/cost tradeoff only — no causal or ablation claim** [paper_1.pdf, p.1][paper_2.pdf, p.1][paper_3.pdf, p.1].

## experiment.xlsx results

The workbook contains a single sheet with 3 rows and 3 columns (`model`, `params_m`, `miou`), no missing values [Analysis 34e957e8-dd44-4233-ad78-920802f6fc85]:

| model | params_m | miou |
|---|---|---|
| A | 2.5 | 73.27 |
| B | 3.2 | 76.0 |
| C | 2.0 | 70.0 |

Across the full set: mean params 2.57M, mean mIoU 73.09, range 70.0–76.0 [Analysis 34e957e8-dd44-4233-ad78-920802f6fc85].

## Best configuration under 3M parameters

Filtering to `params_m < 3` leaves two candidates:

- **A — 2.5M params, mIoU 73.27** ← best
- C — 2.0M params, mIoU 70.0

**Model A is the best configuration under the 3M budget**, beating C by 3.27 mIoU points for 0.5M additional parameters [Analysis 34e957e8-dd44-4233-ad78-920802f6fc85]. Model B is excluded: at 3.2M parameters it exceeds the budget, though it posts the highest raw mIoU (76.0) [Analysis 34e957e8-dd44-4233-ad78-920802f6fc85].

## Chart

A `params_m` vs `miou` comparison chart was generated from experiment.xlsx and saved as **comparison.png** in the workspace [Analysis 34e957e8-dd44-4233-ad78-920802f6fc85].

## Do the results support the reported design advantages?

**Largely yes, but only at the descriptive level — and this is not independent validation.**

Supporting points:
- The experiment values are **numerically identical** to the paper-reported values for all three methods (A: 2.5M/73.27; B: 3.2M/76.0; C: 2.0M/70.0) [Analysis 34e957e8-dd44-4233-ad78-920802f6fc85][paper_1.pdf, p.1][paper_2.pdf, p.1][paper_3.pdf, p.1]. The ordering and gaps confirm the reported tradeoff: A over C by 3.27 points at +0.5M params, and B over A by 2.73 points at +0.7M params — the same arithmetic stated in the papers [paper_1.pdf, p.1].
- The quality-vs-cost pattern (attention > convolution > compact baseline, with monotonically increasing parameter count) is reproduced exactly.

Important limitations:
- Because the workbook values match the paper values exactly rather than differing by any re-measured amount, this is a **replication of the fixture numbers, not an independent re-test**. It cannot confirm that the design choices (attention vs. convolution) *cause* the gains.
- The papers themselves state their claims are **descriptive tradeoff only, with no causal or ablation evidence**, and the fixture provides **three configurations with no uncertainty estimates** [paper_2.pdf, p.1].
- The dataset is a 3-row synthetic fixture, so any conclusion is limited to these three points; there is no statistical power to support generalization.

**Bottom line:** Model A is the best sub-3M configuration (2.5M params, 73.27 mIoU), and experiment.xlsx is fully consistent with the three papers' reported parameter budgets and mIoU figures. The results are consistent with the reported design advantages as a *quality/cost ordering*, but they do not independently validate a causal design advantage, since the values reproduce the fixtures' own numbers and carry no uncertainty estimates.

## Comparison and best configuration

The evidence is a **synthetic Phase 3 fixture, not published research**. It reports Model A: 2.5M params, mIoU 73.27; Model B: 3.2M params, mIoU 76.0; Model C: 2.0M params, mIoU 70.0 [paper_1.pdf, p.1], [paper_2.pdf, p.1], [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. The fixture labels A as convolutional segmentation, B as attention segmentation, and C as a compact convolution baseline; all use the same fixture benchmark/evaluation protocol [paper_1.pdf, p.1], [paper_2.pdf, p.1], [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. It states A improves over C by 3.27 points at 0.5M more params, and B improves over A by 2.73 points at 0.7M more params [paper_1.pdf, p.1], [paper_2.pdf, p.1], [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. Claims are descriptive quality/cost tradeoff only; no causal or ablation claim and no uncertainty estimates are reported [paper_1.pdf, p.1], [paper_2.pdf, p.1], [paper_3.pdf, p.1].

`experiment.xlsx` is 3 rows × 3 columns (`model`, `params_m`, `miou`) with no missing values; its sample is A = 2.5M/73.27, B = 3.2M/76.0, C = 2.0M/70.0 [Analysis af3903c7-a24e-416c-ab49-bcaa84703b03], [Analysis 88faef1d-07be-4472-b83f-7fae1197c8b9], [Analysis 5630ded8-30ff-4cd2-99b8-7b773feef17f].

Computed output ranks by mIoU: B 76.00 > A 73.27 > C 70.00 [Analysis 2b296c03-333b-463b-bcca-96eaf0ae0bb2], [Analysis 5630ded8-30ff-4cd2-99b8-7b773feef17f]. Best under 3M parameters is **Model A** (2.5M, mIoU 73.27); B is excluded because it is over budget at 3.2M [Analysis 2b296c03-333b-463b-bcca-96eaf0ae0bb2], [Analysis 5630ded8-30ff-4cd2-99b8-7b773feef17f]. Among sub-3M models, C has higher computed mIoU-per-million (35.000 vs 29.308 for A), while A is more accurate [Analysis 5630ded8-30ff-4cd2-99b8-7b773feef17f]. Computed Pearson correlation between `params_m` and `miou` is 0.9891; linear trend slope/intercept is 4.9294/60.4380 [Analysis 2b296c03-333b-463b-bcca-96eaf0ae0bb2]. Computed output reports `comparison.png` and `summary.json` saved [Analysis 2b296c03-333b-463b-bcca-96eaf0ae0bb2], [Analysis 5630ded8-30ff-4cd2-99b8-7b773feef17f].

## Do results support reported design advantages?

Numerically, yes for the descriptive tradeoff: spreadsheet values match the synthetic fixture values, including A over C and B over A differences [paper_1.pdf, p.1], [paper_2.pdf, p.1], [paper_3.pdf, p.1], [Analysis 5630ded8-30ff-4cd2-99b8-7b773feef17f]. This does **not** establish that architecture/design caused the improvements: the sources explicitly claim no causal or ablation claim and report no uncertainty estimates [paper_1.pdf, p.1], [paper_2.pdf, p.1], [paper_3.pdf, p.1]. With n=3 and no uncertainty estimates, significance/uncertainty cannot be assessed from these excerpts [Analysis 2b296c03-333b-463b-bcca-96eaf0ae0bb2], [Analysis 5630ded8-30ff-4cd2-99b8-7b773feef17f]. The provided excerpts do not support causal design claims.
